h1: The 6 Best 21-Inch Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six 21-inch cordless lawn mowers from EGO, Greenworks, Worx and SENIX, with plain advice on battery size, drive and mulching.
summary: The Greenworks 80V 21-inch self-propelled mower is the best 21-inch lawn mower: an 80V 4.0Ah battery, a driven wheel set, and a charger in the box, for $200 to $500. The EGO LM2114 is the best push mower on a 56V platform, the SENIX X6 has the biggest 8Ah pack, and the Worx WG752 offers mulch, bag or side discharge.
intro: A 21-inch deck is the standard size because it balances cutting width against storage and handling. Width is the easy part. The real decision is the battery, since voltage and amp-hour rating decide how long you can mow and which other tools the pack will power later. Pick the wrong platform and you buy a second charger when the first mower wears out.

Every mower here is cordless with a 21-inch deck, so we ranked them on battery size, drive type, extras like mulching or height settings, and what each includes in the box. The order comes from listings and from how owners describe these machines, with no runtime figures invented. Packs range from 40V to 80V, and two of the six are self-propelled.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Battery power and a drive system that does the walking for you.
products.description:
This mower pairs the 21-inch deck with an 80V system, a 4.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and self-propelled drive. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. Self-propel is the feature that most changes a mowing session on a larger lot: the wheels pull while you steer, so a long afternoon is less of a slog.

It takes first place because the kit arrives complete. The push version below drops the drive but keeps the same battery, so this is the one to choose if the yard has length or a slope. Against the SENIX X6, it uses a smaller pack but a longer-established brand.

Buy it for medium to larger lawns. The caveat is cost, as you pay for the drive system, and one 4.0Ah pack limits a very large job. Skip it if your lawn is small, flat and easy to push across.
products.idealFor: Medium to larger lawns where walking effort matters.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is small, flat and easy to push across.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2114 21-Inch Cordless Mower
products.verdict: A straightforward full-width push mower on a 56V platform.
products.description:
The LM2114 uses a 21-inch deck on the 56V EGO battery platform, with a push drive and the battery and charger included. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. A 56V platform opens a family of other cordless tools that share the same pack, which lowers the cost of adding a trimmer or blower later.

It places second because it lacks drive, which the Greenworks self-propelled version offers, but it keeps the setup simple for a standard lawn. Its 56V platform lets you add other tools in that family. Against the Greenworks 80V push model, it offers a different tool family at a similar cost.

Choose it for an average, mostly flat yard. The caveat is plain: you push the whole way, and hills get tiring. Skip it if your lawn has slopes or is large.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has slopes or is large.

products.name: SENIX X6 60V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: An 8Ah pack, seven height levels and a smart display.
products.description:
The X6 runs on a 60V system with an 8Ah battery, the largest in this ranking, plus self-propelled drive, seven-level height adjustment and a smart display. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. A bigger Ah figure is simply a bigger fuel tank, which matters on a larger lawn that outlasts a 4Ah pack.

It lands third because it has the best spec sheet but the least established brand here, so there is less owner history to lean on. Against the Greenworks 80V self-propelled, you gain battery capacity and fine height control. Seven height levels let you tune the cut.

It suits buyers who value features over brand heritage. The caveat is that the smart display adds a component that could age, and long-term support is harder to judge. Skip it if you prefer a long-established mower brand.
products.idealFor: Feature-focused buyers with a larger lawn.
products.skipIf: You prefer a long-established mower brand.

products.name: Worx WG752 40V 21-Inch 3-in-1 Mower
products.verdict: Switches between mulching, bagging and side discharge.
products.description:
The WG752 has a 21-inch deck on a 40V platform and offers 3-in-1 operation: mulch, bag or side discharge. The listing rates it for up to half an acre, and it sells in the $200 to $500 range. Mulching returns clippings to the lawn as fertilizer, while bagging suits autumn leaves and weedy turf.

It ranks fourth because the 40V platform is a step below the 56V to 80V rivals, and the listing does not mention drive. The flexibility to change how clippings are handled is the draw. Against the EGO, it offers clipping choices but a smaller battery family.

Choose it for lawns where you mulch in summer and bag in autumn. The caveat is the smaller battery platform. Skip it if you want self-propel or the biggest battery.
products.idealFor: Lawns that need flexible clipping handling.
products.skipIf: You want self-propel or the biggest battery.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 21-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: A larger included battery for flat to gently sloped yards.
products.description:
This Greenworks is a 21-inch push mower on a 60V system with a 5.0Ah battery and charger included. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. A 5.0Ah pack gives a longer session than the 4.0Ah packs on the 80V models, which helps on a gentle slope or a lawn near the half-acre mark.

It ranks fifth because it asks you to push, and the 80V Greenworks models offer similar kit with a different platform. What it offers over the EGO is a 5.0Ah pack, which suits longer sessions on a gentle slope. Against the 80V push mower, it trades voltage for capacity.

Pick it if pack size matters more than drive. The caveat is that it has no self-propel for hills. Skip it if you want drive assistance.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: The 80V platform without paying for self-propel.
products.description:
This Greenworks has a 21-inch deck, an 80V system with a 4.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and a push drive. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. The attraction is the 80V platform, which shares its battery with other tools in that family.

It ranks last because the self-propelled sibling has the same battery and adds drive, and the 60V push mower brings a larger pack. It is a value play for those who want 80V tools. Against the EGO, it matches the push design with a different tool family.

Buy it if you plan to share the battery with other 80V tools. The caveat is that nothing here stands out beyond the platform. Skip it if you want drive or a bigger battery.
products.skipIf: You want drive or a bigger battery.

whatMatters.detail: Volts describe the platform and amp-hours describe capacity, much like a fuel tank. A bigger Ah number means a longer mowing session. Look for both figures in the title or bullets. The SENIX lists 60V and 8Ah, the Greenworks 60V 5.0Ah, and the 80V Greenworks models 4.0Ah. Pack size sets how many square feet one charge covers, so a big lawn may need a second battery.

Self-propelled mowers drive their own wheels, which helps on larger or sloped lawns. Push mowers cost less and weigh less to lift. Check the drive type in the specs. The Greenworks 80V self-propelled and SENIX X6 list drive, while the other four are push or unstated. A driven wheel set also adds weight, so factor in lifting it into a shed.

Buying into a battery family ties future tools to the same brand. That can be good or limiting. Check which other tools use the same voltage. EGO 56V, Greenworks 60V and 80V, SENIX 60V and Worx 40V are different families, so batteries do not cross over. Check the tools you own already before choosing, since a shared pack is the biggest saving.

Mulching, bagging and side discharge each suit different seasons. A 3-in-1 deck handles all of them. Look for the words mulch and bag. The Worx WG752 lists all three, while the other five do not state their clipping modes, so confirm on the listing. Mulching works best on lawns cut often.

More cutting height levels let you tune for grass type and season. Seven levels is finer than the typical few. Look for the level count. The SENIX lists seven, and the others do not state a number. A taller cut helps grass shade its roots in summer, and a lower setting suits spring. Adjustable height is a simple way to adapt to the season.

faq.q: Does a 21-inch deck fit most yards?
faq.a: It suits average yards well. Smaller lots can use a narrower deck, while very large lawns might prefer more battery capacity, such as the SENIX's 8Ah. A wider deck cuts the number of passes but is harder to store.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buying a battery mower?
faq.a: Ignoring the battery platform, which is a long-term decision rather than a mower decision. Voltage decides which other tools you can share it with, so choose a family with the trimmers and blowers you plan to buy. Switching families later means new batteries and chargers.

faq.q: Is self-propel worth the extra cost?
faq.a: On slopes or long lawns, yes, as with the Greenworks 80V self-propelled. On flat small ones, push is plenty and cheaper. Self-propel earns its cost mainly on long runs and mild inclines.

faq.q: Do all of these include a charger?
faq.a: The EGO and Greenworks listings state that the battery and charger are included. Check the Worx and SENIX pages to confirm before ordering. A missing charger can add real cost, so ask the seller.

faq.q: How do I store a battery mower?
faq.a: Keep the battery indoors away from extreme heat or cold, and charge it periodically during off-season storage. Never leave it in a hot garage. Clean the deck after use. Wipe off grass to keep the blade running freely.

The Worx WG752 lists mulch, bag or side discharge. Check others on their pages, since the Greenworks and EGO listings do not name a mulching mode. Mulching also needs sharp blades and frequent cuts to work well.

finalTake: Buy the Greenworks 80V self-propelled for medium to larger lawns and the EGO LM2114 for a flat yard on a 56V platform. Take the SENIX X6 for the biggest battery, the Worx for flexible clippings and the Greenworks 60V or 80V push models for simple value. Decide on the battery platform first, then the drive.
